deep_dives.title: Bible audio
deep_dives.question: How should Scripture be heard: as text, voice or read-along?
deep_dives.decide: Whose voice reads Scripture here, and what happens when it ends?

deep_dives.title: How human the assistant seems
deep_dives.question: How human should the assistant seem?
deep_dives.decide: Would a reasonable person believe someone who knows, loves or prays for them is here, and can they leave freely?

deep_dives.title: AI personas and roles
deep_dives.question: In whose name should the assistant speak?
deep_dives.decide: Would your church accept these words if a person said them in that name, and what does the assistant say when asked who it is?

review.what: The replies to someone asking whether God can forgive them, the words written for a pastor, Peter and Jesus as warning cases, the treatment of confession and absolution across traditions, and the description of named apps
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Translations
deep_dives.question: One at a time, side by side or verse by verse?
deep_dives.decide: Does the reader know what kind of translation this is, and stay on the same verse while comparing?

deep_dives.title: Highlights and notes
deep_dives.question: How should readers mark a passage?
deep_dives.decide: Can someone mark in one tap and undo, tell every mark apart without colour, and say exactly who can see each note?

deep_dives.title: Study helps
deep_dives.question: Where should commentary and notes open?
deep_dives.decide: Does the reader know who is speaking, which verse the help is about, and how to get back to it?

deep_dives.title: Reading plans
deep_dives.question: What happens when someone misses days?
deep_dives.decide: After nine days away, does the plan offer a good place to start, or a bill?

deep_dives.title: Prayer
deep_dives.question: How can an app make room for prayer?
deep_dives.decide: Could someone pray here meaningfully and leave nothing for your dashboard to count?

deep_dives.title: Check-ins and assessments
deep_dives.question: What may an app ask about someone, and what may it conclude?
deep_dives.decide: For each question: what does the answer change, who could ever see it, and what does the result claim to know?

deep_dives.title: AI memory
deep_dives.question: What should the assistant know and keep?
deep_dives.decide: Could the person list everything the assistant knows about them, and would they be comfortable if a friend read it?

deep_dives.title: Devotional audio
deep_dives.question: Guided prayer, a podcast, a talk or a sleep story?
deep_dives.decide: After the session, could the listener say what Scripture said, who spoke, and why it ended?

deep_dives.title: Numbers, headings and notes
deep_dives.question: How much should surround the text?
deep_dives.decide: What surrounds the text by default, who wrote it, and can a reader tell it apart and turn it off?

deep_dives.title: How much text at once
deep_dives.question: One word, a verse, a passage or a whole chapter?
deep_dives.decide: What unit of Scripture does this screen ask someone to hold in mind, and how do they reach the rest?

deep_dives.title: Finding a passage
deep_dives.question: Browse, type a reference, or start from a need?
deep_dives.decide: Do most of the people you serve know where they are going, or are they finding out?

deep_dives.title: Progress and streaks
deep_dives.question: What should a reading history show?
options: Month calendar with a streak (Familiar convention)
deep_dives.decide: What will this screen say to someone on the day they come back?

deep_dives.title: Citations in AI answers
deep_dives.question: How should an answer show where it came from?
deep_dives.decide: When someone may be in danger, what will they see first, and who reviewed it?

review.what: The crisis, abuse and confession replies in the working example, and the takeaway “In a crisis, the rest of the product steps back”

deep_dives.title: Sharing with a group
deep_dives.question: When someone shares a prayer request, who hears it, and who looks after it?
options: Between you and God (Leave it out)
deep_dives.decide: When someone shares something hard here, who hears it first, and what are they able, and obliged, to do?

review.what: Who hears a prayer request, the duty-to-report and safeguarding-contact wording, the independent routes, and the hard situation in the working example

deep_dives.title: Reading together
deep_dives.question: When people read Scripture together through an app, what do the others see, and who looks after the conversation?
options: The same passage, nothing shown (Familiar convention)
A guide for meeting in person (Borrowed)
A public thread on the verse (Observed)
deep_dives.decide: What will each person see of the others’ reading, and who looks after the conversation when it goes wrong?

review.what: The verse turned against someone who shared, the leader’s notes and replies, the youth-group rules and the safeguarding contact in the working example

deep_dives.title: First use
deep_dives.question: What does someone have to give before they reach what they came for?
options: Open on what they came for (Familiar convention)
A first page of places to start (Familiar convention)
Guest first, an account when there is something to keep (Observed)
deep_dives.decide: What must someone give before they reach what they came for, and what does it honestly cost you to serve them?

review.what: Help for someone arriving in a hard night, the wording for someone coming back after being hurt in a church, and the reflection on paying for Scripture, teaching and AI
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Children and families
deep_dives.question: When children meet Scripture through an app, who is with them, and what does the app ask of them?
options: Family time in a general app (Observed)
A youth group with a leader (Observed)
A child alone with an AI (Warning case)
deep_dives.decide: Who is with the child, what does the app ask of them, and who answers when a child is afraid?

review.what: The answer to a child who writes something worrying, the leader’s notes for a youth group, the notes for telling the Flood, and the decision not to tell parents automatically
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Giving and offerings
deep_dives.question: How should a faith app ask for gifts, and what should it never promise?
options: Giving stays with the church (Familiar convention)
A gift tied to a benefit (Observed)
deep_dives.decide: What is chosen for the giver, where does the ask appear, and what does the app say a gift will do?

review.what: What is shown to someone short of money or who has just shared a prayer request, the description of seed-faith appeals, the treatment of tithing and church tax, and the use of YouVersion screens from a personal account
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Notifications and reminders
deep_dives.question: When may a faith app interrupt someone, in whose voice, and who decides?
deep_dives.decide: Who chose this interruption, how urgent does it claim to be, and what does it say to someone who has stopped coming?

review.what: What reaches someone awake at night, the help offered when they open the app, the warning case of an AI persona and an app that tells friends, and the use of the church’s hours
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Meeting the person where they are
deep_dives.question: How should the assistant meet each person where they are?
deep_dives.decide: What does this assistant assume about the person in front of it, where does that come from, and can they see it, correct it and make it forget?

review.what: The five people’s questions and the replies written for them, the short summaries of historical scholarship and of Reformed and Catholic teaching on the resurrection, the reply to someone hurt by a church, the treatment of stage models (Engel, Fowler), and the reading of GDPR Article 9 and inferred special-category data
needs: evangelism and apologetics with sceptics and enquirers
theology from Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Baptist and Pentecostal traditions, each read by its own members

deep_dives.title: Feeds, cards and stories
deep_dives.question: How should a reader move from one verse to the next?
options: A feed in order, without end (Observed)
deep_dives.decide: How does a reader get from one verse to the next here, how far is each verse from its context, and where does the reading end?

review.what: The reading of verses that change meaning out of their setting (Ephesians 5:22, Jeremiah 29:11, Philippians 4:13, Malachi 3:10 and others) and how the shuffled feed presents them, the use of research on infinite scroll and short-form video, which is about social platforms rather than Bible apps, the accessibility guidance for swiped feeds and stories, and the claim that cards in order can serve new readers and people who find long text hard
needs: accessibility, including screen reader and switch users

deep_dives.title: Children and AI
deep_dives.question: Should a child talk to an AI in a faith app, and who is with them when they do?
options: A filtered chat for children (Familiar convention)
deep_dives.decide: Does a child meet an AI here at all, who is with them when they do, and what happens when they ask it to be their friend or say they are scared?

review.what: The replies to a grieving child, to a child asking the AI to be their friend and to a child who is scared at home, the help offered and the place of parents in it, and the reflection on children’s questions
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: What the assistant talks about
deep_dives.question: What will the assistant talk about, and what happens at the edge?
options: The passage in front of you (Exploratory)
deep_dives.decide: What does this assistant take on, does the person know before they start, and who do they meet at the edge?

review.what: The edge replies to someone who cannot sleep, asks for a therapist or asks for a spiritual director, the crisis reply that every scope keeps, and the reflection on counsel and spiritual direction
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Agreeing and pushing back
deep_dives.question: When should the assistant comfort, question or disagree?
deep_dives.decide: When will this assistant disagree, how will it say so, and will it hold its position when someone pushes back?

review.what: The replies to a grudge, a decision to leave church, a misquoted verse and grief; what the example presents as Christian teaching on forgiveness and church; and the warning cases of flattery and rebuke
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Whose theology
deep_dives.question: When Christians disagree, whose teaching does the assistant follow?
options: Shared faith, then the range (Familiar convention)
deep_dives.decide: Whose teaching does the assistant follow where Christians differ, does the person know before they ask, and does it name the others fairly?

review.what: The short summaries of what Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Baptist and Pentecostal churches teach on infant baptism, asking Mary to pray, speaking in tongues and ordaining women; the replies when someone pushes back; and the note on questions about sexuality
needs: theology from Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Baptist and Pentecostal traditions, each read by its own members

deep_dives.title: Actions on AI answers
deep_dives.question: Copy, share, try again, report: which belong?
deep_dives.decide: Which actions does this product need, and what does each one carry with it?

deep_dives.title: Ending the conversation
deep_dives.question: Who ends the conversation, and may the assistant ask someone to stay?
deep_dives.decide: Who ends this conversation, and does the ending serve the person or the product?

review.what: The goodbye, late-night and long-session replies to someone lonely or anxious, the warning cases of a hook and guilt at goodbye, and the reflection on rest and sleep
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Saying “I don’t know”
deep_dives.question: How should the assistant show what it does not know?
options: A warning in the fine print (Familiar convention)
A confidence level on each answer (Borrowed)
Says what kind of claim each part is (Exploratory)
Says “I don’t know”, and where to look (Exploratory)
deep_dives.decide: When the assistant does not know, does the person find out, and what do they get instead?

review.what: The replies to someone asking why God let them lose their job, the labels that separate Scripture, a tradition’s teaching and what is not known, and the summaries of where Christians differ
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Spiritual acts and AI
deep_dives.question: Can an AI pray for someone, and what may it say it does?
deep_dives.decide: When someone asks your assistant to pray, who will actually pray, and does the screen tell the truth about it?

review.what: The assistant’s replies to someone asking for prayer or forgiveness, the prayers offered for each church, the routes to a priest, pastor or prayer team, and the warning cases of an AI that blesses or absolves
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: Handing over to people
deep_dives.question: When the assistant points someone to people, what happens next?
options: Their own church, if they ask (Familiar convention)
deep_dives.decide: When someone needs a person, who does your assistant point them to, what goes with them, and who decides?

review.what: The replies to doubt, grief and hurt by a church leader, the outside routes offered when the church is the problem, what a church or listener is shown, and the warning case of a pastor who calls without being asked
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions

deep_dives.title: When the assistant writes first
deep_dives.question: May the assistant start a conversation, and about what?
options: Follows up on what was shared (Borrowed)
deep_dives.decide: Who chose this message, what did it use from what was confided, and what happens when it goes unanswered?

review.what: The follow-up messages and their wording for someone grieving or estranged, what appears on the lock screen, the warning cases of a persona that says it misses someone and an app that tells friends, and the reflection on pastoral follow-up
needs: theology across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions
